sources.entry: pint - Operate and manipulate physical quantities with units and dimensional analysis.

summary.one_liner: Pint is a Python library for defining, operating on and converting physical quantities (a numeric value paired with a unit), with dimensional analysis and NumPy support.
summary.what_it_does: Pint lets you create quantities by multiplying numbers with unit objects from a UnitRegistry, then perform arithmetic and conversions between compatible units (for example, adding meters and centimeters). It ships with a built-in list of physical units, prefixes and constants, and the list can be extended by editing a text definition file without changing code. Unit parsing recognizes prefixed and pluralized forms of defined units, so "kilometers" works once "meter" and "kilo" are defined. It supports NumPy arrays and ufuncs with automatic unit handling, including unit checks such as requiring a dimensionless input for arccos. The README also mentions string formatting (PEP 3101 plus symbolic, LaTeX and pretty output), temperature scale conversions, uncertainties integration, Pandas extension types, and a pint-convert command-line script.
use_cases: convert between units of length, mass or temperature
do arithmetic on values that carry units
check dimensional consistency of scientific calculations
apply NumPy operations to arrays with units
use units in Pandas DataFrame columns
convert units from the command line
notable: Unit definitions live in an editable text file, so units can be added or changed without touching source code
Prefixed and pluralized unit names are understood automatically from base definitions
NumPy ufuncs and methods work with unit conversion without monkey patching or wrapping numpy
Handles temperature conversions between scales with different reference points
Any numeric type can be used, including float, Fraction, Decimal and ndarray
caveats: Full documentation is hosted externally; the README gives no details beyond the links
